facts.claim: Ho, Jain and Abbeel’s 2020 paper (DDPM) made high-quality pictures with a diffusion model. It set T = 1,000 steps for all its experiments, so sampling one picture runs the network 1,000 times.
Song and colleagues (2021) describe a diffusion model as noise added gradually and then removed in reverse: “Creating noise from data is easy; creating data from noise is generative modeling.”

Classifier-free guidance (Ho and Salimans, 2022) trains one model with and without the label, dropping it at random, and mixes the two predictions as (1 + w) × labelled − w × unlabelled, trading sample diversity for quality.

The 2022 latent diffusion paper notes that the most powerful pixel-space diffusion models often took hundreds of GPU days to train (150–1,000 V100 days), and about 5 days on one A100 to make 50,000 samples.

Latent diffusion (Rombach et al., 2022) runs the denoiser on a pretrained autoencoder’s smaller latent picture, shrunk by a factor f each way; the paper found f of 4 to 16 a good balance, with 4 and 8 best.

Flow matching (Lipman et al., 2023) trains on paths from noise to data; its optimal-transport paths run in straight lines where diffusion’s curve, which the authors report gives faster training and sampling.
Consistency models (Song et al., 2023) map noise to a picture in one step, can take a few steps for better quality, and can be trained by distilling a diffusion model.

Carlini and colleagues (2023) showed that diffusion models memorise individual training images and emit them when generating, extracting over a thousand training examples from state-of-the-art models.
